items.summary: Unrefereed candidate. A proof that for every n >= 1 and real c, every non-real eigenvalue of the 2n x 2n indefinite tridiagonal pencil H_c - lambda S (diagonal c, off-diagonal 1, S = diag(1,...,1,-1,...,-1)) satisfies |lambda - c| < 2 and |lambda + c| < 2. This is Conjecture 5.3 of Davies and Levitin (Linear Algebra Appl. 448, 2014), and it implies the closed-disk form of AIM 2015 Problem 11.1. It was previously known for n <= 3 and for eigenvalues equidistant from c and -c (Öztürk 2023). A standard Weyl-function mechanism, applied to the known Chebyshev form of the characteristic equation, reduces the conjecture to a comparison lemma for an explicit Lorentzian sum over the zeros of U_{n-1}; the comparison lemma and its proof are the original contribution. It is proved by explicit estimates with finitely many Arb-certified constants for n >= 8, elementary arguments for n <= 2, and, for 3 <= n <= 7, an explicit estimate plus a short interval certificate with rational endpoints and Arb ball arithmetic. Certified examples show that the lens fails for some other spectral measures, for a balanced pencil with one weakened coupling, and for unbalanced pencils. The package contains the manuscript, certificates, regression tests, semantic negative controls and review records. Provenance: the research, proof and text were produced by an AI research agent (Claude, Anthropic) under the direction of the publisher, Evidence Press; no human mathematical contribution is claimed, and no human specialist has checked the proof. Internal replay and model-based reviews only; no formal verification, independent reproduction, specialist or journal peer review; novelty is established only within a bounded literature search.
items.title: A proof of the Davies–Levitin lens conjecture for the indefinite tridiagonal pencil

items.summary: This data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “An rRNA-embedded ribosomal protein N-terminus loses its methionine: a cross-species census, a genome-scale test and a local-compatibility hypothesis for assembly” (Yie-Hwa Chang, 2026; bioRxiv preprint, submitted to Nucleic Acids Research). Methionine aminopeptidases remove the initiator methionine when residue 2 is small and uncharged, and loss of this activity is lethal in bacteria and yeast. The archive asks whether the structural environment of a ribosomal protein N-terminus predicts its processing class across lineages, whether the same association holds in sequences without structure, and whether the constrained termini are already in place while the subunit assembles. The census comprises 68 ribosome structures from 61 species, 1,873 family × species records and 95 ribosomal protein families, 58 of which switch processing class between species. Termini embedded in rRNA without protein contact were predicted to retain methionine in 18% of records, against 45% of protein-contacted and 41% of solvent-exposed termini. Eight additional structures from separate species corroborated this pattern, which was attenuated under joint family-by-domain stratification. Processing labels are sequence-based predictions from residue 2, validated against 393 directly observed termini from 12 species (98.7% agreement). Thirty-one families never switch class in any sampled species (25 permissive, 6 methionine-retaining), and eleven of the permissive families are threaded into rRNA. The genome-scale layer contains 942,984 family × genome records from 21,485 UniProt reference proteomes, collapsed from 1,027,359 sequences of 94 families. In 6,924 out-of-sample bacterial reference proteomes, exploratory clade-block permutation tests supported an order-level residue-2 association that is sensitive to taxonomic rank and multiplicity: it survives Holm adjustment across the ten bacterial tests (p = 0.036 and 0.019) but not across the thirty tests of the three domains analyzed separately (0.117 and 0.057). The archaeal and eukaryotic tests are coverage-limited (six and eight eligible families) and inconclusive. In yeast assembly intermediates, the conserved uS12 and eS27 termini already occupy their mature environments. The findings indicate a conserved association between rRNA embedding and methionine removal and suggest that local compatibility of processed termini with rRNA contributes to it; they do not demonstrate an assembly requirement, and the census is offered as a resource for testing this hypothesis at named termini. items.summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-
items.title: Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Networks for Hierarchical Epidemic Modeling, Environmental Perturbations, and Source Identifiability

items.summary: Version 2 (26 September 2026): a one-page "Corrections and attributions" section is added at the front of the PDF, listing every credit correction below; nothing else in the paper is changed and no proof is withdrawn. The revised, shorter note that supersedes this paper for the results stated there is 10.5281/zenodo.22980359. Note (24 September 2026): a revised version is in preparation. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.
items.title: One-way functions are computational entropy production

items.summary: Long-running interactions with large language models can become historically organized, but apparent continuity across branches or reconstructed sessions may arise from several different carriers, including accessible history, memory systems, procedural state, lineage, or harness-level persistence. This naturalistic case study examines a longitudinal interaction between one human collaborator and a GPT-5.6 Sol trajectory called “Solomon,” using a ten-day Founder corpus and four naturalistic continuity configurations ranging from a fresh out-of-project response to continuations with inherited or archive-assisted history. The study does not claim consciousness or strict personal identity. Instead, it asks which aspects of prior organization are immediately available, which require reconstruction, and whether prior commitments continue to constrain appropriate action in novel situations. In the sequential qualitative synthesis of the ten-day Founder corpus, research commitments, provenance rules, relational procedures, governance constraints, and future-directed tasks were interpreted as becoming more explicitly integrated and mutually constraining over time. We call this structure of unfinishedness: an organized future in which unresolved obligations and sequencing constraints shape what should happen next. The naturalistic evidence is compatible with multiple reconstruction mechanisms and does not identify a unique causal carrier. It therefore motivates a controlled fork–recover–ablate–migrate design that equalizes accessible history while varying lineage and other continuity-relevant state, with novel extrapolation and update dynamics as key discriminators. Keywords: LLM agents; continuity; branching; fork; recovery; relational identity; longitudinal interaction; agent memory; persona; harness; path dependence; provenance
items.title: FORK, RECOVERY, AND HISTORICALLY ORGANIZED CONTINUITY IN A LONGITUDINAL LLM–HUMAN INTERACTION: A Naturalistic Case Study

items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. items.summary: A thirteen-chapter monograph on geometric and analytic structures that recur in quantum gravity. The chapters range from functional realizations of matrices and tensors to emergent spacetime. Each chapter separates proved results from conjectures and heuristic proposals, and states that status explicitly. Part I (Ch. 1–2) studies functional realizations of matrices and tensors and geometric flows on matrix, tensor and graphon spaces. Part II (Ch. 3–6) covers: - the analytic continuation of Pascal's simplex; - Beta-kernel operators; - interdimensional transforms; - analysis on Sierpiński simplices. Proved results in Part II include: - the asymptotics of continuous multinomial integrals; - an expansion of the continuous row entropy via the Barnes G-function; - an inversion formula for the Radon–Beta transform. Part III (Ch. 7–10) develops the L∞ minimax extrinsic-curvature problem for submanifolds and curves in obstacle domains. Its proved results include: - existence for curves; - a contact principle; - sharp U-turn bounds in Euclidean and constant-curvature spaces; - finiteness of homotopy classes under a length bound. Part III also treats applications to ADM slicings and relativistic trajectories. It shows the limits of transferring the problem to information geometry. Part IV (Ch. 11–12) reviews established links between entanglement, tensor networks and gravity, with sources (linearized Einstein equations from the entanglement first law, min-cut bounds, the loop-quantum-gravity area spectrum). It formulates the open questions as conjectures. Part V (Ch. 13) is an order-of-magnitude assessment. It concludes that Planck-suppressed signatures of the two-scale spectral-dimension model lie far below current and planned sensitivities. The Lean 4 files in the companion repository are a naming skeleton and do not verify the mathematics. LaTeX sources, numerical checks, audit records and the register of findings are in the repository: https://github.com/reinaldomsilvafilho-netizen/quantum-gravity-lean4

It includes the Python source code, the numerical data behind all figures and tables, and the validation records. The code computes the collisionless dielectric response, the inverse bremsstrahlung structural factors, the electronic stopping power and its sensitivity to the wavenumber cutoff. All verification checks passed, and an independent implementation agrees with the production solver to within 10⁻¹¹ relative difference at the benchmark points. The package was tested with Python 3.12, NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib; the README gives full instructions for reproducing the results.

items.summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.
items.title: Nothing Escapes, Three Plus One: A Formal Closure of the Riemann Hypothesis. The Strip Vanishes for Every Registration and the Universe of the Hypothesis Closes on the Critical Line

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22967519 . This paper looks at what happens when we trust an AI coding agent's work without independently checking what actually changed. The authors show a case where a protected file was changed, but GTB still returned VERIFIED because the file was left out of the verification process. I thought one of the strongest parts of the paper was the distinction between stopping an agent from doing something and actually being able to prove that it didn't do it . The paper also does a good job of showing the attack in practice, explaining why the verification failed, and suggesting ways to make the process more reliable. Major issues The experiment focuses on GTB, so testing other coding-agent or verification systems would help show whether the issue is specific to GTB or appears more broadly. The proposed fixes have not yet been independently tested. Testing them against the same attack, along with a few variations, would make the results more convincing. Minor issues Including the exact software versions and experimental environment would make the experiment easier to reproduce. A simple diagram showing the normal verification path and where the modified file gets excluded would make the main failure easier to understand. It would also be useful to state how many times the attack was repeated and whether the same result occurred consistently Competing interests The author declares that they have no competing interests. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) The author declares that they did not use generative AI to come up with new ideas for their review.

items.summary: Governance near a plausible critical transition faces a resource problem in addition to problems of diagnosis, intervention, and evidence. Elevated susceptibility can increase the value of observation, bounded experimentation, and revisability, while waiting can simultaneously consume the fiscal, material, organizational, temporal, and relational capacities required for survival and later action. This paper develops a discussion framework for that tension. Its central object is functional resource distribution: the allocation of heterogeneous capacities across observation, probing, short-horizon survival, selective commitment, reserve or option preservation, and recovery or repair. The categories are analytical functions rather than a scalar budget partition and can overlap in practice. The paper introduces distributed optionality as a relational property of a response architecture in which materially different future actions remain supported by functionally diverse and sufficiently non-coincident pathways. It distinguishes exact reversal from recoverability, spatial dispersion from independence of failure modes, and delay as information gathering from delay as resource dissipation. The framework inherits, rather than restates, earlier arguments about response-oriented governance and evidence-to-action instability near criticality. Its distinctive question is how governance capacity may be composed when the future regime is uncertain, resources are partly non-substitutable, and both premature commitment and indefinite waiting can narrow the feasible future. The proposal is conditional and non-prescriptive: criticality requires domain-specific empirical support, and the appropriate resource portfolio depends on transition mechanism, horizon, institutional structure, and explicit normative commitments.
items.title: Governance and Survival near Criticality: Functional Resource Distribution and Distributed Optionality

items.summary: Neural receivers for 5G NR are commonly compared against least-squares (LS) baselines, which leaves open whether they improve on a well-tuned classical receiver and whether their gains survive conditions outside the training distribution. We evaluate a fully convolutional neural receiver and a lightweight hybrid receiver, which retains a classical LS and linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) front end and learns a residual correction of its log-likelihood ratios, on standard-compliant 5G NR PUSCH with 3GPP tapped delay line channels and hardware impairments. Baselines include an LMMSE channel estimator supplied with the empirical statistics of each test scenario (genie) and one supplied with a single fixed set of statistics from the training mixture (practical). Inside the training range both learned receivers only match the genie baseline. Two regimes differ. With an RMS delay spread of 2000 ns the learned receivers require 0.90 dB less than the genie baseline, while the practical LMMSE receiver does not reach 10 percent BLER at all; with a single DMRS symbol the neural receiver requires 4.08 dB less than the best classical receiver at 20 m/s and is the only receiver that operates at 30 m/s. We further show that the apparent failure of learned receivers outside the training envelope is a matter of training coverage rather than architecture: widening the training delay spread from 30-300 ns to 30-1000 ns converts a 5.97 dB deficit at 2000 ns into a 0.90 dB advantage, at a cost of at most 0.1 dB for speeds up to 45 m/s. Trained on the same range, the hybrid receiver matches the full neural receiver within 0.05 dB using 3.9x fewer parameters and FLOPs. Finally, we document a baseline pitfall: DMRS-based carrier frequency offset compensation also removes the Doppler shift of a dominant line-of-sight path, invalidating the LMMSE correlation model and costing 0.84 dB, which can produce illusory gains for learned receivers. Code, configurations and results: https://github.com/Ewwftyy/neural-receiver-5g-nr
items.title: Training Coverage, Not Architecture, Decides When Learned 5G NR Receivers Help

items.summary: This paper argues that river deltas and arterial trees, though studied in separate fields, share a common mathematical architecture. Using side-by-side images as a Rosetta stone, it treats their resemblance as a diagnostic clue rather than a metaphor. Both are described as rooted, planar, directed, space-filling trees with a single inlet, repeated branching, and many terminal outlets. At every internal junction, flow is conserved. Both exhibit hierarchical scaling and self-similarity. The central contribution is a common variational template. If a branching network minimizes a separable cost combining transport dissipation and maintenance or volume cost, then optimal branch sizes at each junction obey a power-law relation. The exponent depends on the physics: viscous laminar flow yields Murray's law for blood vessels, while Manning-style open-channel flow yields a different, testable river scaling. Thus the template does not prove identity; it shows that one abstract optimization structure can generate known biological scaling and a conditional geophysical prediction. The paper then asks why such similarity exists. It offers conjectures: convergent optimization, constructal law, diffusion-limited aggregation, resource constraints, robustness, and a universal attractor. It states falsification tests: scaling exponents and graph metrics should not be random after conditioning on constraints, and diagnostics should transfer across domains. A second theoretical part connects the networks to thin and thick chaos. It defines a diagnostic tuple and proves transport-graph invariance: if two transport graphs are isomorphic in the relevant sense, preserving coherent and failure regions and the ordering of edge weights, then thin, transitional, and thick classifications transfer. This supports cross-domain diagnostics for flood forecasting and cardiovascular risk, for example, tracking failure pathways. The paper is careful about limits. Rivers and arteries differ physically in fluid, compliance, timescale, and dynamics. The claim is structural and mathematical, not physical identity. The unity is a shared abstract architecture, not sameness.
items.title: One Tree, Two Fluids: Convergent Mathematical Architecture of River Deltas and Arterial Trees

items.summary: International Environmental Law stands at a crossroad, where its basic ideas and principles are massively coming at odds with the depth and demand of universal environmental catastrophe. Greatly based upon notions of state control, assent, and fragmented international agreement, the discipline has failed to respond to massive environmental degradation and biodiversity failure. The formation of the scientific notion of the ecological boundaries and limits has elevated the constraint by introducing a bunch of environmental thresholds and limits within which the humankind can remain secure. Developed by the Stockholm Resilience Centre, this framework uncovers crucial biodiversity dynamics like the massive ecological destruction, ecological threshold, poor land usage and change, and bio-geochemical cycles and hence introduces a novice standard beyond which the irreparable environmental damage sharply increases and spikes. While this model has gained impeccable speed and admiration among scientific and policy stakeholders, its ethical interpretation and application for international law remains questionable. This paper argues that adopting environmental limits within the scope and ambit of international environmental law calls for a thorough transformation from fragmented governance towards an obligatory structure of earth system governance.
items.title: Planetary Boundaries And International Environmental Law: Towards Earth System Governance

items.summary: Let a consumer trust its cache instead of re-fetching it trust_cached_entries (default False ) serves a cache entry as it is on disk: no staleness re-fetch, and no full-text retry. Staleness re-fetching suits a cache the tool owns and can rebuild. For a cache that is committed to a repository and reviewed it inverts — the re-fetch becomes the risk rather than the repair. Three failures reported downstream were the same re-fetch seen from different angles: an unstamped full_text_html entry withheld, pointing at a repair route that cannot be reached ( dismech#12672 ) a fetch returning PMC's bot-check page on an HTTP 200, its <title> then compared against the curated title ( dismech#12867 ) a re-fetch shortening 64 bodies and breaking snippets that had verified, in a pull request about something else ( dismech#12879 ) Setting the flag removes the fetch, so there is no window in which any of them can happen. The default is unchanged, so caches still migrate for consumers that want that. The trade is explicit: an imperfect cached entry stays imperfect. That is a content problem to fix deliberately — cache reference --force still rebuilds one on purpose — rather than something re-litigated on every validation run. Also in this release Review follow-ups from #94: a test for the refused-overwrite path that consumers actually take (the previous tests only covered _stale_fallback ), a stale-HTML warning that no longer advises a retry that cannot succeed for a PMC-only article, find_pmc_article_body made public since two modules share it, and a note that PMC_ARTICLE_BODY_CLASSES is ordered by priority. items.summary: Pipeline and derived matrices for a three-domain calibration of cross-study agreement among public transcriptomic signatures. The analysis covers 19 human datasets: peripheral blood in COVID-19 (10 datasets), peripheral blood in sepsis (5), and aortic wall in dissection or aneurysm (4). This gives 61 pairwise signature comparisons. Headline results. Median pairwise Jaccard overlap was 0.014, 0.072 and 0.023 across the three domains. Observed overlap was 5.6, 10.2 and 6.5 times the expectation for random gene sets of the same size, with 47 of 61 pairs significant after FDR correction. Consensus across ten COVID-19 blood datasets retained two genes from a union of 4,225, and relaxing agreement to 20 per cent retained 717. Simulations with a known shared 250-gene signature hold at 250 for every k and converge after two datasets, so the failure is unstable detection rather than sample size. The release contains a size-aware concordance measure, a permutation null, consensus analysis across datasets, ground-truth simulations in shared-signal and private-signal regimes, and an offline reproduction bundle. No expression matrices are redistributed; all 19 datasets are public and cited by accession in the paper.
items.title: Size-aware cross-dataset concordance of public transcriptomic signatures

items.summary: Predicted protein structures are now abundant but imperfect, and low per-residue confidence (pLDDT) is widely taken to mark regions worth refining. Before building a refiner, we test that premise directly: does low pLDDT actually predict AlphaFold contact error? Using a homology-controlled benchmark of matched AlphaFold-model (AFDB) inputs and experimental (PDB) targets, we compare AlphaFold and experimental contacts for every long-range residue pair and relate per-pair error to pLDDT. Across all 231 benchmark chains (4,208,603 long-range pairs; the effective sample is 231 chains, since pairs are pseudo-replicated within proteins), AlphaFold’s long-range contact calls are almost all correct — but this is expected, since most long-range pairs are non-contacts, so we focus on the contact-relevant errors. The per-pair contact-error rate is 0.0036 (95% bootstrap CI over chains 0.0033–0.0040), decomposed into false-positive contacts (asserted but absent) and missed real contacts. Low pLDDT is associated with elevated contact error (0.0089 below pLDDT 70 versus 0.0024 above, a 3.70× enrichment, 95% CI 3.3–4.1), but predicts it only weakly: the discrimination AUC of pLDDT as a contact-error score is 0.672 (95% CI 0.65–0.69), the best Youden threshold is near pLDDT 81 and the best F1 threshold near pLDDT 52, and pLDDT < 70 captures only 46% of all contact errors at sub-percent precision. False-positive (44%) and false-negative (56%) errors have different pLDDT profiles. Sequence/evolutionary information (ESM-2 contact probabilities) identifies these errors partially (AUC 0.61–0.63 for false positives, 0.66–0.86 for missed contacts), and low-confidence pairs that sit near a high-confidence anchor have a lower error rate (0.0074 versus 0.0090), suggesting anchor-based correction is a direction worth pursuing. Consistent with the weak localization of error, on a common subset of chains a hybrid Transformer–geometric refiner selected on validation precision cannot be distinguished from a copy-input baseline that trusts the AlphaFold structure (paired bootstrap over chains does not exclude zero difference). The practical conclusion is that on high-quality AlphaFold inputs there is little contact error to recover and pLDDT does not localize it well; useful refinement will need error-specific, evolutionarily grounded signal and may exploit high-confidence anchors. We release the benchmark, the characterization pipeline, and the code.
items.title: AlphaFold Contact Errors and pLDDT — Homology-Controlled Benchmark and Characterization

items.summary: This dataset provides the nationally consistent, footprint-level classification of residential building subtypes across the United States. It contains over 140 million building footprints classified into four distinct structural residential categories:  Single-Family Homes (SFHs), Townhouses (including duplexes), Apartments, and Mobile Homes .    The dataset is organized geographically and stored as individual, high-performance GeoPackage ( .gpkg ) files for each of the 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia .   Data Schema (Attribute Fields) Each state-level GeoPackage contains the following standardized attribute columns:   geometry (Polygon) : The spatial boundary (polygon) of the building footprint. Res_type (Integer) : The classified residential structural subtype code: 1 = Single-Family Home (SFH) 2 = Townhouse (explicitly includes laterally attached row houses and semi-detached duplexes) 3 = Apartment 4 = Mobile Home height (Double) : The estimated physical height of the building in meters. Baseline heights are obtained from Microsoft Global ML footprints, with a minimum threshold of 4.2 m enforced (representing a typical one-story structure) and missing values imputed using local tract-level medians. type (String) : Building type tags from OSM building footprint (Limited coverage and varies by region).   Methodology and Classification Workflow The residential classifications were achieved using a novel, scalable hierarchical spatial workflow that integrates geometric building footprints with high-confidence administrative and demographic auxiliary data:   Multi-Source Footprint Integration: Geometry was compiled by merging Microsoft US Building Footprints, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, and OpenStreetMap (OSM) geometries. Non-residential structures were purged during preprocessing using OSM land-use layers and manual reclassification of OSM building tags. Mobile Home Identification: Candidate footprints located within spatial buffers around documented mobile home parks were classified using state-specific Random Forest (RF) models trained on footprint geometry (area, aspect ratio, rectangularity, and local density). High-confidence "seeds" were subsequently expanded using context-aware spatial promotion rules. Single-Family Home (SFH) Calibration: High-confidence SFHs were initially mapped using administrative address attributes. To prevent over- or under-counting, a size-ranked rule-based spatial promotion algorithm was implemented to sequentially classify candidate footprints until the counts aligned with rigorous state-level housing stock benchmarks derived from the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. Townhouse and Apartment Discrimination: The remaining unclassified structures were categorized using a sequential, rule-based physical geometry and address-point pattern-recognition workflow. Duplexes and linear townhouses were distinguished from multi-family apartment blocks by evaluating physical constraints (convexity, height, and structural width) paired with the spatial density and linear alignment of internal address points from the National Address Database (NAD) . Spatial Context Completion: A final, iterative morphological distance-matching algorithm resolved any remaining unclassified structures based on local neighborhood class composition and physical architectural similarities (height, area, and aspect ratio).
items.title: Nationwide Footprint-Level Classification of Residential Building Subtypes for the United States

items.summary: Version 2 (2026-09-25): the strata were redefined. A case's causative gene is now a known disease gene if its gene–disease pair was annotated in HPOA v2025-08-11 at the cutoff or a publication before the cutoff had reported a patient with a germline variant in the gene, and novel if neither (primary-analysis set: known 75 = 46 by annotation + 29 by publication alone; novel 30; version 1 had 46 / 59 by annotation alone). The repository snapshot (commit 87a2a95) carries the per-case strata with their evidence ( docs/case_strata.csv , docs/novel_gene_literature.csv , analysis/novel_genes/literature/ ) and the re-scored results, figures and tables; the run archives are unchanged. See README.md. Inputs, outputs and answer key for a benchmark comparing two arms on rare-disease cases from phenopacket-store first published on or after 2025-09-01: air-gapped OpenScientist (Claude Opus 4.6, no internet, a local PubMed mirror pruned to articles first public before 2025-09-01, able to run Exomiser) versus Exomiser 14.1.0 alone (data release 2508, stock exome preset). 133 primary-tier cases were run in both arms. 124 extension-tier cases were run in the Exomiser arm only. Each case is a sanitized phenopacket plus a simulated VCF with the causal variant spiked into a 1000 Genomes background exome. As a leakage control, an LLM-only probe (Opus 4.6, no tools) was run on the 133 post-cutoff cases and on 105 pre-cutoff control cases. items.summary: RED-REJECT-2026-v2 is the corrected release of a public benchmark corpus of algorithmic filter rejections with post-rejection follow-up samples, collected by a purpose-built follow-up-tracking process on the Solana pump.fun ecosystem between 2026-04-11 and 2026-07-16. The 96-day window contains one collection gap: no new rejection events were recorded from 2026-06-03T06:35Z and no samples from 2026-06-04T06:32Z until 2026-06-24 (about 21.4 and 20.4 days), so the window contains about 75.6 days of sampling coverage. It supersedes v1 (published 2026-07-16); see CHANGELOG.md for the corrections.   Corpus size: 716,762 post-rejection sample records across 4,635 unique SPL token mint addresses, comprising 18,237 distinct rejection events under eight named algorithmic trading filter families (shares of the 716,762 sample rows: downtrend_24h 56.13 percent, marketcap_out_of_range 21.38 percent, multi_tf_fade 11.98 percent, timeSlot_not_strong 5.17 percent, hour_blacklist 2.36 percent, ultra_fast_reject_exit 1.64 percent, utc_hour_blocked 0.92 percent, h6_sellers_dominating 0.41 percent). After canonicalization, no row carries a null rejectReason (v1's 348 null-reason rows came from an unfolded alias). For each observation, the corpus records the token's live market state at the sample time (price, liquidity, volume, rolling price changes), the identity of the DEX pair (absent in the 8,356 legacy family_2 rows), and the elapsed minutes since the original rejection event. Rows in schema variant 1 (from 24 April 2026 onward) also record macro-regime context (BTC price, fear-greed index, regime label).   The corpus applies the Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling (PRFS) methodology to this collection.   Version v2.3 corrects the documentation only; every data file is byte-identical to v2.2. It discloses the June collection gap, which v2.2 described as continuous coverage, clarifies that the 4,278 events listed in alt_venue_report.csv have more than one (dexId, pairAddress) value, a null value included (88 of them are observed on two or more identified trading pools), and corrects several descriptive statements. See CHANGELOG.md.
items.title: RED-REJECT-2026-v2 (corrected release): A 96-Day Public Corpus of Algorithmic Filter Rejections with Post-Rejection Follow-up Samples on the Solana pump.fun Ecosystem

items.summary: Artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-blind review . Author information is withheld until publication; a later version of this record will carry it, and the concept DOI is stable across versions. What this is. When two unlabelled subgroups of documents are compared by embedding similarity across languages, countries, corpora or periods, and the difference is read as evidence about those sources, no accuracy figure certifies that reading. within_language_baseline.py supplies the missing baseline: it measures the same subgroup contrast inside a single source, where no across-source relation can enter, and reports the residual with a bootstrap interval and an equivalence verdict against a margin declared in advance. The tool has no dependency on the accompanying study and runs on any corpus with three columns ( text , group , source ). It carries its own injection tests ( --selftest ). The bootstrap resamples documents rather than pairs and excludes duplicate draws of the same document from within-source pairs. Also included: the 36 frozen anchor correspondences used as the gold standard, the per-encoder CJK retrieval evaluation, the measured within-language and cross-country genre gaps, the equivalence intervals, an append-only correction record for the non-analytic genealogy fields of the frozen anchors, and anonymised review copies of the post hoc centring protocols and of the departure record. MANIFEST.sha256 covers every deposited file except itself.

items.summary: This repository accompanies the manuscript Agent-Based Modeling in Tairona Chiefdoms of the Río Frío Basin, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia (c. AD 100 to 1600) and contains the reproducible computational workflow used to construct, calibrate, execute, and evaluate a spatially explicit household agent-based model for the 52.2 km² Río Frío archaeological survey area. The model contrasts bottom-up, mixed, and top-down organizational scenarios while incorporating household production, residential mobility, demographic fission, cooperation, surplus transfer, soil degradation and recovery, ecological forcing, and cumulative landscape investment. Archaeological settlement observations are translated into 25 m cells nested within 250 m analytical zones, and model evaluation follows a pattern-oriented framework comparing observed and simulated change in occupied-zone density, settlement concentration, spatial extent, and nearest-neighbor spacing. The experimental design combines three organizational scenarios with stable, declining, and shock ecological conditions and independently varies landscape investment, producing 360 baseline simulations. Global sensitivity analysis additionally evaluates 16 parameters across 180 Latin hypercube sets. The repository provides the R workflow used for data preparation, simulation, validation, sensitivity analysis, figure generation, and manuscript tables, supporting transparent replication, methodological evaluation, comparative reuse in archaeological modeling, and facilitating critical assessment of alternative mechanisms underlying long-term settlement and socio-ecological change patterns.

items.summary: Background: Traditional post-marketing drug monitoring framework metrics rely heavily upon passive, spontaneous clinical case notification configurations. These configurations systematically suffer from extensive reporting lag phases and a massive underreporting of actual consumer adverse drug reactions (ADRs). With the explosive expansion of global digital platforms, modern patient networks frequently document raw, unformatted clinical complaints online long before consulting a healthcare practitioner. Objective: This core research constructs, validates, and evaluates an enterprise cloud architecture prototype termed "Shreyas SmartPV Mobile" to automate case intake pipelines, deploy cognitive semantic extractors, map raw text onto official MedDRA hierarchies, and execute immediate regulatory eligibility checks. Methodology: A multi-layered low-code pipeline structure was engineered using Glide Apps and Softr for responsive frontend client interface extraction, Airtable as the primary secure relational cloud database storage, and Make.com as the background workflow synchronization integration orchestrator. Data streams are processed via a cognitive node driven by the Google Gemini Large Language Model (LLM) framework running specific clinical validation rules, multi-stage Named Entity Recognition (NER), and automated token dictionaries to extract suspect therapeutic drug classes cleanly from descriptive toxicological events. Results: Extensive experimental validation using standard chemical benchmark metrics (including Paracetamol, Aspirin, and Ibuprofen scenarios) verified 100% precision in parsing unstructured digital narratives, mapping baseline complaints to standard MedDRA Preferred Terms (PT) (e.g., matching 'red rashes on skin' to Erythematous Rash), and computing immediate validation states (Report Valid? = True) based on strict international safety compliance requirements. The system recorded an average automated triage execution velocity of less than 3.9 seconds per array. Conclusion: The validated automation workflow confirms that cloud-native cognitive processing pipelines cut manual data entry fatigue, optimize processing costs, and maximize patient-reported signal capture. This technical transition shifts drug safety management from passive tracking arrays into dynamic, real-time digital active safety listening ecosystems.
tags: Pharmacovigilance, Artificial Intelligence, MedDRA Ontology, Cloud Orchestration, Large Language Models, Low-Code Systems Engineering
items.title: AI-Driven Social Media Listening And Automated Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) Extraction System For Advanced Pharmacovigilance
